# 1: Project Overview

This project acts as window into the relationship between a powerlifter's bodyweight and their overall strength. Will a powerlifter's bodyweight be directly correlated with compound lifts (squat + deadlift + benchpress)? This project will focus on cleaning the data set, seperating genders, identifying age classes, weight classes, and graphing the information to see strength standard trends. 

-----

## 2.2.1: Data Set Information & Fair Use

**Producer and authority.** OpenPowerLifing.org hosts an open-source, non-profit collection of power lifting data. It is published as an open data-set to standardize global power lifting meet results into a single easy-to-use domain.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The purpose of OpenPowerLifting.org is to preserve power lifting data taken from professional meets and to provide a comprehensive archive of athletic accomplishments. It is primarily utilized to track rankings and analyze sport trends among athletes.

**Collection method.** The values are gathered manually through official power lifting organizations using power lifting federation score sheets and score-reporting platforms. The data provided is analyzed and structured into a CSV file.

**Coverage and resolution.** This data set is globally covered through multiple officially licenced power lifting federations. This data dates as far back as 1964 to today through continuous competition results.

**Licence.** Creative Commons Zero (CC0 1.0 Universal) Public Domain Dedication, allowing unrestricted use, modification, and distribution for any purpose.

**Access.** Downloaded directly from OpenPowerLifting.org public git. Accessed through OpenPowerLifting.org/data.

**Known problems.** After a brief look through, some values are missing. Some figures that are required for my project appear to have a null value such as Best3SquatKg, Bench, and Deadlift. Some body weight is also missing.

# 4: Consent and identifiability

**Consent.** This data provides the users with individual human powerlifter's details such as names, sex, and age. The data is sourced from open athletic competition results that are public records. In order for these athletes to compete they must meet under federation rules that record key identifiers such as names, weights, performance statistics, and doping tests. For the purpose of this project names will not be used in any graph or collective.

**Identifiability.** This data set is publicly recorded through athlete sport statistics and utilizes information like competition names, body weights, and strength numbers through power lifting competitions. Because these records are shared publicly, individual identification is based entirely on publicly available results from competitions. However, for this project names will not be used, but key characteristics of athletes will be analysed

**How sensitive data will be used.** Although the OpenPowerLifting data set has names and competition data this project will be analyzing strength standards on a population level rather than an individual level. Names and specific athletes will **not** be singled out. all information found in this project will be used in figures such as summary tables, regression models, and graphs. This will ensure that no individual identity is highlighted.

## 5.2: Who could be harmed

Misuse of this data would include external companies that might affect individuals found in these competitions. Companies that revolve around insurance or employment. Misusing this data could result in false conclusions regarding physical wellness, workplace compatibility, or insurance rate adjustments. 

## 5.3: Unreleased working data

Due to this data set being public through CC0. It is entirely safe to publish my project. This project will be almost exclusively relying on Bodyweightkg, and Totalkg. There is no unreleased working data in this project that needs to be withheld.
